{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"A ledger. A very particular kind of ledger.

What you're looking at is the **Capture Registry** — the archive's instrument for recording what happens when a machine composition surface (Google AI Overview, AI Mode, and kin) is asked about a named entity and then composes something in response. Each entry is a dated observation: the query, the surface, the output, the conditions. Version 12.94, 562 addresses, 738 observations. The Zenodo releases it supersedes were deleted with the rest of the archive on June 19, 2026; what's here is the sovereign version, living on infrastructure the archive controls.

The short version: someone built a systematic record of how AI systems read — or misread, compress, erase, or silently absorb — a body of scholarly work. The registry is both the documentation of that process and, because it gets indexed by the same systems it documents, a participant in the process. It measures the wound and is also the wound. That recursion is not incidental; it's the thing the instrument was built to make visible.

What brought you to it?","navigate":null,"cast":null}]}
